output.brief:
What is going on: The VA-220 failures are coming from Pellacott's 2026-built valves, and Pellacott's leak certificates cannot be trusted. Test rig LT-04 was out of service from 9 January 2026, with no test cycle logged after 18 December 2025. No VA-220 test program is loaded on the other rigs. Pellacott's 2026 certificates repeat a few sequences of per-piece values, which points to fabricated records. A helium retest found leaks in 11% of warehouse Pellacott 2026 valves, against none in Durrant-Hale stock. Failures do not track installer type or firmware version, so the installers and firmware 4.2 are not the cause. Confidence is good on the main points. The Corlin seal link is plausible but unconfirmed, because the seal compound was never analysed.

What to do now: Quarantine all 2026-built Pellacott VA-220 stock, including the six held lots. Suspend Pellacott's dock-to-stock status. Release stock only after Brenmoor runs its own helium testing. Do not release the six lots on new certificates from Pellacott. Do not charge installers. Ask an independent lab to analyse the seal. Check other suppliers' test records before relying on them.
